title: AI agents just doubled inside the enterprise. Confidence rose faster than control did
source_used: Gravitee sponsored post on TechCrunch (TC Brand Studio, paid content)
key_facts: The article is paid content by Gravitee, an API and AI-agent management vendor; TechCrunch editorial was not involved.
Gravitee's State of AI Agent Security 2026 report surveyed 750 executives and technical leaders in April 2026 against a December 2025 baseline.
The typical enterprise agent deployment rose from 26-50 agents to 76-100 in one quarter.
Mean monitoring coverage went from about 47% to about 52% while stated confidence in visibility rose from 82.6% to 91.8%.
54% of organizations experienced or suspected an agent security or privacy incident in the past 12 months; telecoms 67.3%, financial services 54.7%.
85% have no formal accountability structure for agent behavior; only 7.2% name a responsible individual.
81.7% plan to deploy more agents in the next 12 months.
quote_evidence: This article is presented by TC Brand Studio. This is paid content, TechCrunch editorial was not involved in the development of this article.
Gravitee, an AI Agent Management company, surveyed 750 executives and technical leaders in April 2026 and layered the results on top of a December 2025 baseline.
85% of organizations have no formal accountability structure for AI agent behavior, and only 7.2% can point to a named individual responsible when an agent acts.
why_it_matters_hint: A vendor survey says companies are deploying agents far faster than they monitor them, which fits the pattern of incidents reported elsewhere.
event_date: Survey April 2026; report release date not stated
notes: Sponsored content by a vendor selling agent-governance tools; survey data is from April 2026; no independent review. Treated as a vendor report, not news reporting.
